changes.text: The Creator now has a Sound Set catalog where you can browse, preview, and install sound sets into your project as ordinary assets.
You can audition a Sound Set through the player before installing it, and stop the audition from the same surface.
Sample slicing now offers suggested slice candidates you can preview and adopt into pads, with cancellations and adoption history preserved across sessions.
The core engine gained a global Pattern transport: acknowledged live pattern switching with cutoff reconciliation, loop overdub recording, and durable recovery of interrupted recordings.
The Creator adopts the global Pattern transport, so live pattern switching and overdub recording stay consistent while you play.
The web player integrates the global Pattern transport runtime surface.
The Creator's hardware console was rebuilt on the Figma 15 design: the hardware layout is now the default, and the Perform, Sample waveform, Project list, and Sequence screens were restyled.
The Cardputer handheld host gained its display, keyboard, and audio lifecycle adapters, resource diagnostics, and a USB transfer protocol with identity expiry, assembled as a test build.
The core engine can export and read back bounded runtime content, and the player reports peak voice levels observed while stopped.

Creator hardware console polish: Record and Play use the correct colors, encoders and keys sit on their intended tracks, hardware icons render under the content security policy, Pad Capture grips are centered, and the Sample waveform playhead advances during playback.

Creator capture and editing fixes: the capture panel survives audio recovery, waveform trim handles are available, a stale replay poll no longer overwrites the final state, and the project format level guard is enforced correctly.

Pattern transport reliability fixes: retained events are committed when a recording closes, owner-lost recordings appear in the recovery listing, and stale transport projections no longer linger after a switch.

The audio engine uses less memory and CPU: immutable sample data is shared across runtime sample banks, queues and voice-state storage are bounded by actual receipts, per-frame scans skip silent voices, and capture storage is allocated on demand.
Audio engine stability fixes: a Sound Set audition can no longer crash the web player, and playback publication ordering and synchronization semantics are preserved.
Cardputer host fixes: keypad presses decode on the correct edge, codec gain and DAC startup are corrected, transfer acknowledgements are fully validated, and receive-side memory is bounded.
Storage failures are clearer and safer: error messages name the refusing step and the unreadable project copy, and the Sound Set Store leases its destination before publishing.

Web player fixes: the Sound Set catalog is reached through a same-origin forward with bounded parsing, auditions report whether they actually played, and the bundle levels the product packs are accepted.
Project Bundle format versions v1 through v4 are retired and no longer accepted; projects saved in those formats must be migrated with an earlier build.
New projects are written in the lmdj.project.v4 format (now at 4.1.0 with Sound Set lineage), and asset inventories created by 2.x builds are still accepted as prior identities.
The pinned toolchain for building the core engine moved from Clang/LLVM 18 to Clang/LLVM 22.

changes.text: The Creator has a collapsible developer diagnostics panel, reachable in every mode, that keeps the last 100 errors of the current workspace with their operation, UTC time, code, message, and details; switching modes keeps the list, reloading the page clears it, and nothing is stored or uploaded.

Recording over a looping Pattern on the global Pattern transport is now audible while you record: what you play into one pass comes back on the next pass instead of only after Record is switched off, and Record-off and live Pad input keep responding while that pass is queued.

A take interrupted mid-recording, for example by reloading the page, can now be recovered: applying an owner-lost Pattern transport recording restores the take you heard, with any still-held Pad press ending at its default length, instead of refusing it.

Starting two Performance recordings on the same project at once is reliably serialized: a contender can no longer mistake a recording that has just started for an abandoned one, and a refused start no longer leaves an active recording journal behind for a Performance that was never saved.

The Sample workspace no longer shows its own duplicate Bank row and Pad grid: Bank selection and the playable Pads live only on the left hardware rail, which now also handles Pad selection, empty-slot sample picking, and drag-and-drop replacement, and Sound Set installation uses a separate Install target Bank that does not change the Bank you are playing.
Open or create a Project at startup, and create or duplicate Projects from the library.
Add session Undo/Redo through the SHIFT rail controls; deleting Pad sounds preserves the rhythm.
Edit Pad reverse, pitch, pan, loop mode, attack, release, tone and three-band EQ through the shared audio engine.
Show and edit the Sequence grid with gestures and Undo/Redo, with atomic Pattern event editing in Core and the Web Host.
Control Tempo/Swing directly, use Tap Tempo, and enable a metronome that is excluded from recordings.
Apply Perform FX with press gestures without requiring a Performance recording session.
Wake browser audio on the first musical gesture without a dedicated activation gate.
Stream an original 16-Pad default drum set from an independent asset service, verifying and installing each slot separately.
Record an empty Pad immediately on press and finish on release; first microphone permission prepares the next press.
Move settings, MIDI, Provider management and diagnostics into System while retaining the four music pages.
Refresh the stage shell, brand/favicon, colours and console typography, with a centred layout and bounded scrolling.

Define the four-role Stem PCM16 contract and durable proof Provider; shared content retains distinct port roles. This is contract/replay proof, with real model quality still outside the delivered proof.
Restore the last Project after a crash, support explicit takeover from another tab, and ask whether to retain interrupted recordings on reopen.
Explain Project, Sample, import, capture, Slice, Sound Set, Perform and Undo errors with actionable user-facing messages.
Allow Pad Delete, Reset, Mute and Replace while audio is inactive.
Fit the Sequence overview/grid to their displays and anchor the playhead to observed Runtime frames.
Load the AudioWorklet graph on a parked context and handle output-device startup refusal without sealing the session.
Preserve an active Performance replay across Host publications and keep Runtime state current across settings changes.
Preserve default streaming across owner loss and keep cached offline recovery consistent with the Host favicon inventory.
Reduce deep Web stack copies of ProjectState and restore build compatibility after cross-feature integration.
Advance lmdj.project.v5 through compatible 5.1 and 5.2 updates for the current authoring capabilities.
Propagate coordinated P1 Host identities and derive offline/package/deployment asset inventories from the actual Creator version.
Recover receiver-owned transfer display state for the Cardputer Host; physical hardware acceptance remains separate.

P1 device and subjective-audio acceptance remains deferred in Issues 1851-1854: real microphone/Master capture and replay, offline reopening, iPad touch/lifecycle, and physical MIDI. Native Chrome/Safari GUI observations are partial evidence. This release makes no beta/stable or hearing-acceptance claim.

changes.text: Reorganize Sample, Perform and Sequence into contextual pages with a unified Graphite control language, consolidated status and recovery controls, mode-specific overview context, touch-bar Sequence views and guided Sound Set installation.

Redesign the console shell for Desktop Final: Project, Sample and Perform upper screens, A01-D16 Pad addressing, eight scrollable Sequence track rows, EDIT and SETUP touch layers, Sequence encoders and direction keys, bundled IBM Plex Mono, fitted centred scaling and System behind the brand mark.
Arrange Pad matrices from the bottom left, draw one user-chosen Pad colour on every surface, and persist Pad colours and categories in Projects.
Resize, double and copy Patterns through Core, the Web Host and SETUP.

Switch Patterns while the transport plays: bind pending Pattern cutoff and Record opening, switch the transport at the next Bar, configure playing switch boundaries and fence named switches against the playing generation.

Add live Performance controls: a one-admission live-control kernel with a durable Project profile and admission ledger, live Pad Mute/Solo gating with shared-FX tail preservation, and an independent live Filter branch with typed cutoff and resonance.
Share device monitor volume with Perform MASTER, add contextual encoders and a capture-independent monitor output.
Map keyboard rows 1234/QWER/ASDF/ZXCV to pad rows and reserve keyboard shortcuts from Pad input.
Edit Sample parameters precisely and unify the current Pad across Sample and Sequence.
Cut lmdj.project.v5 5.3.0 to 5.4.1 with Pad colours and categories, the live-control profile and the canonical input_sequence anchor.
Activate Cloudflare Portal previews under a bounded monthly hosted budget.

Align the touch interaction layouts across Interaction, Slice, Numeric, Sequence setup, Import Audio, Sound Sets, Capture, Trim, Playback, Pad palette and recovery, and expose live Pad mute and solo controls.
End unreleased terminal owners instead of waiting forever and stop retained polling after a terminal owner ends.

Align Performance Pattern Launch with the transport origin, preflight direct replay profiles before effects, enqueue replay neutral gates before the gesture burst, retain landed overlay authority before cutoff, stop JSON parsing at the depth limit and serialize Creator inspections through an owned Session.

Preserve musical position across tempo changes (#2155), expose the typed Performance live-control producer on the Web Host (#2083), publish retained Pad assignments (#2107), consume the typed Filter and FX groups in the Creator (#2139), keep the full liveness deadline for a late Performance event (#2336), anchor the audio clock to the first native render (#2360), retain actual Pattern switch publication boundaries (#2362), and persist continuous recording segments with their ordering (#2364, #2365).

Preserve ready history across page navigation, keep Performance Launch closed during transitions, avoid aliasing live bar observation windows, cancel queued switches from the current Groove and keep transport reconciliation with the current command.

Fit touch controls within fixed panels, synchronize touch and overview previews, name only the real Perform gate in its disabled label, refresh queued authoring commits at their committed revision, configure Catalog for local serving and align the hardware keyboard hint with the spatial mapping.

Stop replay before transport and Project changes, preserve stopped Pattern transport authority, observe selection after a completed callback, measure monitor energy on matched frames, route retained transport retries through the facade, adopt the observed recording admission cursor and wait out an in-flight paused callback when activating audio.

Report applied state on exact live-control retries, count headered Performance FX gestures, isolate render CPU and validate Master FX accounting, cut live-gated Pad input immediately and flush the checkpointed source tail before a Pattern switch.
